stem: Which type of communication flows **between departments at the same level** of a business?

options.content: Horizontal communication between peers
options.rationale: Correct: it passes between people or departments of equal rank.

options.content: Downward vertical communication from managers
options.rationale: This passes from managers to subordinates.

options.content: Upward vertical communication from workers
options.rationale: This passes from workers to managers.

options.content: One-way communication to customers
options.rationale: This describes a message to outsiders with no reply.

explanation: Horizontal (lateral) communication links people at the same level, such as the production and sales managers.

stem: Which of the following is an example of **informal** communication?

options.content: Colleagues discussing a rumour at lunch
options.rationale: Correct: it passes outside the official channels.

options.content: A written warning to an employee about lateness
options.rationale: A written warning follows official procedure.

options.content: The minutes of the annual board meeting
options.rationale: Minutes are a formal record.

options.content: A memo from the manager to all the staff
options.rationale: A memo is an official written message.

explanation: Informal communication (the grapevine) passes through personal contact, not the official lines of authority.

stem: What is the main feature of **two-way** communication?

options.content: The message goes to exactly two receivers only
options.rationale: The number of receivers does not matter.

options.content: It is always written and always formal in style
options.rationale: It can be spoken and informal.

options.content: The receiver sends feedback back to the original sender
options.rationale: Correct: feedback is what makes it two-way.

options.content: It is sent by two different managers in turn
options.rationale: The number of senders is not the test.

explanation: Two-way communication includes a reply, so the sender can check understanding.

stem: A fictional factory in Gweru has seven levels of management. Which problem is MOST likely to result from the long chain of command?

options.content: Messages travel faster than in a flat structure
options.rationale: Each extra level adds delay.

options.content: Messages are slow and may be changed on the way
options.rationale: Correct: each level can filter or distort the message.

options.content: Every worker speaks directly to the owner
options.rationale: A long chain separates workers from the owner.

options.content: Feedback is always instant and complete
options.rationale: Feedback travels back through every level.

explanation: A long chain adds delay, filtering and distortion.

stem: A manager sends a ten-page technical report to shop assistants. Which barrier to communication is MOST likely?

options.content: Excellent feedback from the staff
options.rationale: Feedback is not a barrier.

options.content: Perfect timing and a short message
options.rationale: The report is long and technical.

options.content: Jargon and information overload
options.rationale: Correct: the language and the volume are unsuited to the receivers.

options.content: A very short chain of command
options.rationale: The chain is not the issue here.

explanation: Technical language and a large amount of information make the message hard to understand.

stem: Workers at a fictional quarry in Masvingo hear a rumour that wages will be cut, although management has said nothing. Which action BEST reduces the damage of the rumour?

options.content: Punish the workers who repeated the rumour in public
options.rationale: This increases mistrust and does not supply the facts.

options.content: Hold a meeting to give the facts and take questions
options.rationale: Correct: accurate, two-way information replaces the rumour.

options.content: Ignore it, because the grapevine cannot matter at all
options.rationale: Ignoring it lets the rumour spread.

options.content: Send a one-line text and refuse to take any questions
options.rationale: One-way communication leaves doubts unanswered.

explanation: The grapevine is best met with timely, accurate, two-way communication.
hints: Which action supplies facts and allows feedback?

stem: A fictional bus company in Mutare sends route changes by a notice on the head-office board. Drivers work in depots 150 km away. Which change would BEST improve communication?

options.content: Add more notices to the board at the head office
options.rationale: Distant drivers still cannot see them.

options.content: Wait for the drivers to ask about route changes
options.rationale: This is slow and leaves errors.

options.content: Use longer and more technical wording in each notice
options.rationale: This makes understanding harder.

options.content: Message the group, then confirm by phone
options.rationale: Correct: it reaches distant depots and checks understanding.

explanation: A message the drivers can receive, with a check on understanding, deals with distance and the lack of feedback.
hints: Think of distance and of feedback.

stem: A manager of a fictional 12-person tuck shop wants to spend two hours a week on staff meetings to improve communication. Which statement is the BEST evaluation?

options.content: Meetings are always worth their cost in every business
options.rationale: The value depends on the size and the problem.

options.content: Meetings cannot improve communication in any firm
options.rationale: They give two-way contact and can help.

options.content: Cost is irrelevant when communication is involved
options.rationale: Time and cost matter to every decision.

options.content: The gain may be small in so small a team, so the cost needs weighing
options.rationale: Correct: in a small firm informal talk may be enough.

explanation: A judgement should weigh the benefit against the cost for this business.
hints: Look for the answer that links the benefit to the size of the firm.

stem: Downward communication passes from managers to subordinates.
explanation: True. Instructions, targets and policies flow down the hierarchy.

stem: A manager can remove the grapevine completely by banning informal conversation.
explanation: False. Informal communication arises from human contact and cannot be banned; managers reduce rumour by giving accurate, timely information.

stem: Match each barrier to the example.

right.content: The mobile network is down, so branches cannot be reached
Workers doubt every announcement because of earlier broken promises
Staff who speak Shona receive instructions only in technical English
A supervisor receives 60 emails a day and misses the safety notice

explanation: Each barrier prevents the message being sent, received or believed.

stem: Choose the correct word for each gap.

payload.template: Communication between a manager and a worker is {{blank:a}} communication, while communication between two department heads is {{blank:b}} communication.

explanation: Vertical communication runs up and down the hierarchy; horizontal communication runs between people at the same level.

stem: State the term for informal communication passing between employees outside the official channels.
explanation: The grapevine is the informal network by which news and rumour pass.

stem: State **one** barrier to communication that is caused by a worker's fear of speaking to a senior manager.
explanation: Differences in status or culture, and the attitudes that follow from them, stop workers passing on information or problems.

stem: Explain **one** disadvantage of a long chain of command for communication in a business.

points.description: Messages pass through many people
Each person may filter or change the message, so it is distorted
Decisions are slow and managers at the top may lack accurate information

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: In a long chain of command a message passes through many people. Each may leave out or change some detail, so the message is distorted, and decisions are slow because information takes a long time to travel.

explanation: A disadvantage developed to a consequence.
hints: Think of each level in the hierarchy.

stem: A fictional clothing factory in Bulawayo has staff who speak different home languages, and the supervisor gives instructions only in English. Explain **two** ways in which this barrier could harm the business.

points.description: Some workers may not understand the instruction
Application: they could sew a garment wrongly, wasting cloth
Staff may feel excluded and less motivated
Application: morale falls, causing lower output or higher labour turnover

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Some workers may not understand an instruction given only in English, so they might sew a garment wrongly and waste cloth. Staff may also feel excluded, which lowers morale and could reduce output or raise labour turnover.

explanation: Two effects, each applied to the factory.
hints: Link the barrier to waste and to motivation.

stem: Analyse how two-way communication could improve the efficiency of a fictional bakery in Harare when it introduces a new oven.

points.description: Workers can ask questions about the new oven
Mistakes in using it are reduced
Staff can pass on problems or ideas to managers
So less wasted bread, less downtime and faster output

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: With two-way communication bakers can ask questions about the new oven, so fewer mistakes are made in using it. They can also report problems and suggest improvements to management. This reduces wasted bread and downtime and speeds up output, improving efficiency.

explanation: A chain from feedback to efficiency.
hints: Link feedback to mistakes and then to output.

stem: A fictional chain of six hardware shops in Zimbabwe plans to spend US\$20,000 on a new communications system and weekly briefings. Evaluate whether this is a good decision.

points.description: Benefit: fewer errors and clearer instructions across the six shops
Benefit: faster decisions and better coordination of stock and prices
Benefit: staff feel informed and more motivated
Cost: US\$20,000 and management time each week
Cost may not be recovered if the problems are small or lie elsewhere
Judgement with a reason or condition, e.g. worthwhile if mistakes are currently frequent and costly

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A new system and weekly briefings should reduce errors and give clearer instructions across the six shops, speed up decisions and keep staff better informed and motivated. However, US\$20,000 and weekly management time are significant, and the benefit is small if the existing problems are minor or lie elsewhere. The decision is worthwhile if errors are frequent and costly; otherwise a cheaper step, such as regular phone briefings, may be enough.

explanation: A balanced judgement in context.
hints: Weigh the benefits against the cost, then give a judgement with a condition.

stem: Read the extract. Tatenda Textiles is a fictional clothing firm in Gweru. The owner sends all instructions by a written notice on the factory wall. Workers have no way to reply. Last month a notice changed the length of a school uniform, but a third of the workers did not see it, and 400 uniforms had to be re-cut.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: State the type of communication used by the owner (one-way or two-way).
parts.explanation: The notice gives no planned feedback, so it is one-way.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Identify **two** barriers to communication shown in the extract.

points.description: The method reaches only those who see the notice (poor medium)
No feedback, so misunderstanding was not found

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A notice reaches only those who see it, and workers have no way to reply, so misunderstanding is not found.

parts.explanation: Poor choice of medium and no feedback.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain **one** way in which the owner could improve communication.

points.description: Hold a short daily team briefing or use group messages
Workers can ask questions and confirm understanding
So fewer mistakes and less re-cutting of cloth

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The owner could hold a short team briefing each morning. Workers could ask questions and confirm what they have heard, so fewer uniforms would have to be re-cut.

parts.explanation: A suitable two-way improvement developed to a result.

explanation: One-way; poor medium and no feedback; a briefing gives two-way contact.
hints: Think about feedback and about who saw the notice.

stem: Read the extract. A fictional courier company, Zambezi Express, has a head office in Harare and depots in Mutare, Bulawayo and Victoria Falls. Decisions are made by head office and passed through depot managers and supervisors to drivers. Drivers say they hear about route changes late, and depot managers say head office ignores their suggestions. A rumour that the Victoria Falls depot will close has spread among staff.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Explain **one** problem caused by the long route that messages take from head office to drivers.

points.description: Messages pass through several people
Each may delay or change the message
Drivers receive route changes late or in the wrong form

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Messages pass through depot managers and supervisors before reaching drivers. Each may delay or change the message, so drivers hear of route changes late or in a different form.

parts.explanation: Delay and distortion on a long chain.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Analyse **one** way in which the rumour about Victoria Falls could affect the company.

points.description: Staff at Victoria Falls fear job loss
They may work less hard or leave
Service to customers falls or recruitment costs rise

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Staff at Victoria Falls fear losing their jobs, so they may work less hard or look for other jobs. Service to customers would fall and the company would face the cost of recruiting and training replacements.

parts.explanation: A chain from rumour to cost.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Recommend **one** change to improve upward communication and justify it.

points.description: A recommendation, such as regular depot visits or a suggestion system
Managers' ideas reach head office directly
Justification: decisions are better and managers feel valued

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Head office should hold a monthly video meeting with depot managers. Their ideas would reach head office directly, so decisions would be better informed and managers would feel valued and less likely to leave.

parts.explanation: An upward channel with a reason.

explanation: Delays on a long chain; the effect of rumour; an upward channel improves decisions.
hints: Look at the direction of each problem: down, up and informal.
